title: 5 Moments in History That Sound Fake (But Really Happened)
description: Five true stories that sound made up: the Emu War, the Dancing Plague of 1518, the Great Molasses Flood, the man who sold the Eiffel Tower, and Hiroo Onoda.

scenes.text: March 1974.
scenes.say: [serious] March 1974.

scenes.text: A Japanese soldier walks out of the jungle in a tattered uniform.
scenes.say: A Japanese soldier walks out of the jungle in a tattered uniform.

scenes.text: His rifle still works.
scenes.say: His rifle still works.

scenes.text: And as far as he knows... World War Two is still going on.
scenes.say: And as far as he knows... World War Two is still going on.

scenes.text: That really happened.
scenes.say: [curious] That really happened.

scenes.text: And it's not the only story today that sounds made up.

scenes.text: An army that lost a war... to birds.

scenes.text: In 1932, wheat farmers in Western Australia had a big, feathery problem.
scenes.say: [curious] In 1932, wheat farmers in Western Australia had a big, feathery problem.

scenes.text: About twenty thousand emus had marched out of the outback and into their fields, eating everything.
scenes.say: About twenty thousand emus had marched out of the outback and into their fields, eating everything.

scenes.text: So the farmers asked the government for help.
scenes.say: So the farmers asked the government for help.

scenes.text: And the government sent... the army.
scenes.say: [excited] And the government sent... the army.

scenes.text: A major named Meredith, two machine guns, and ten thousand rounds of ammunition.
scenes.say: A major named Meredith, two machine guns, and ten thousand rounds of ammunition.

scenes.text: On paper, this should have taken an afternoon.
scenes.say: [confident] On paper, this should have taken an afternoon.

scenes.text: It did not.
scenes.say: [chuckles] It did not.

scenes.text: The moment the guns fired, the emus scattered in every direction.
scenes.say: The moment the guns fired, the emus scattered in every direction.

scenes.text: The soldiers set an ambush at a watering hole, and a huge flock walked right toward them.
scenes.say: The soldiers set an ambush at a watering hole, and a huge flock walked right toward them.

scenes.text: They got about a dozen birds. Then the gun jammed.
scenes.say: They got about a dozen birds. Then the gun jammed.

scenes.text: They even mounted a gun on a truck, but the ground was so rough that nobody could aim.
scenes.say: They even mounted a gun on a truck, but the ground was so rough that nobody could aim.

scenes.text: After about a week, the soldiers were called home.
scenes.say: After about a week, the soldiers were called home.

scenes.text: Meredith later said that if he had a division with the bullet-carrying capacity of these birds,
scenes.say: Meredith later said that if he had a division with the bullet-carrying capacity of these birds,

scenes.text: it could face any army in the world.
scenes.say: it could face any army in the world.

scenes.text: The farmers begged again, so the army went back for round two.
scenes.say: [curious] The farmers begged again, so the army went back for round two.

scenes.text: In the end, Meredith's report claimed nine hundred and eighty-six emus...
scenes.say: In the end, Meredith's report claimed nine hundred and eighty-six emus...

scenes.text: using nine thousand eight hundred and sixty bullets.
scenes.say: using nine thousand eight hundred and sixty bullets.

scenes.text: Exactly ten bullets per bird.
scenes.say: [laughs] Exactly ten bullets per bird.

scenes.text: Newspapers called it "the Emu War."
scenes.say: Newspapers called it "the Emu War."

scenes.text: And the emus? Still there. Still eating the wheat.
scenes.say: And the emus? [amused] Still there. Still eating the wheat.

scenes.text: The army had lost a war to birds.
scenes.say: The army had lost a war to birds.

scenes.text: Birds beating an army is funny.
scenes.say: [softly] Birds beating an army is funny.

scenes.text: What happened in one European city, four centuries earlier... was not.
scenes.say: What happened in one European city, four centuries earlier... was not.

scenes.text: July 14, 1518. Strasbourg.
scenes.say: [mysterious] July 14, 1518. Strasbourg.

scenes.text: A woman named Frau Troffea stepped into the street and started to dance.
scenes.say: A woman named Frau Troffea stepped into the street and started to dance.

scenes.text: No music. No reason.
scenes.say: No music. No reason.

scenes.text: She danced all day, until she collapsed.
scenes.say: She danced all day, until she collapsed.

scenes.text: The next day, on swollen, bleeding feet, she danced again.
scenes.say: [uneasy] The next day, on swollen, bleeding feet, she danced again.

scenes.text: By the end of the week, more than thirty people had joined her.
scenes.say: By the end of the week, more than thirty people had joined her.

scenes.text: Within a month, some accounts say, four hundred.
scenes.say: Within a month, some accounts say, four hundred.

scenes.text: People who wanted to stop... and couldn't.
scenes.say: People who wanted to stop... and couldn't.

scenes.text: The city's doctors blamed "hot blood," and their cure was simple: more dancing.
scenes.say: [curious] The city's doctors blamed "hot blood," and their cure was simple: more dancing.

scenes.text: So the city built a stage, hired musicians, and paid people to keep the dancers moving.
scenes.say: [sighs] So the city built a stage, hired musicians, and paid people to keep the dancers moving.

scenes.text: It made everything worse.
scenes.say: It made everything worse.

scenes.text: Some old records claim dancers collapsed and even died, though historians still argue about how many.
scenes.say: Some old records claim dancers collapsed and even died, though historians still argue about how many.

scenes.text: Finally, the city changed its mind.
scenes.say: Finally, the city changed its mind.

scenes.text: Music was banned, and the dancers were taken to a shrine in the hills to pray.
scenes.say: Music was banned, and the dancers were taken to a shrine in the hills to pray.

scenes.text: Slowly, the dancing stopped.
scenes.say: Slowly, the dancing stopped.

scenes.text: So what was it? Nobody knows for sure.
scenes.say: [whispers] So what was it? Nobody knows for sure.

scenes.text: Many historians think it was mass panic, in a city worn down by failed harvests, record grain prices, and disease.
scenes.say: Many historians think it was mass panic, in a city worn down by failed harvests, record grain prices, and disease.

scenes.text: Fear spread from person to person, until it took over their bodies.
scenes.say: Fear spread from person to person, until it took over their bodies.

scenes.text: A whole town, dancing, and not one of them wanted to.
scenes.say: [softly] A whole town, dancing, and not one of them wanted to.

scenes.text: That town couldn't stop moving.
scenes.say: [tense] That town couldn't stop moving.

scenes.text: Four hundred years later, in Boston, something else started moving... and it weighed about thirteen thousand tons.
scenes.say: Four hundred years later, in Boston, something else started moving... and it weighed about thirteen thousand tons.

scenes.text: January 15, 1919. Boston's North End.
scenes.say: [calm] January 15, 1919. Boston's North End.

scenes.text: It was strangely warm for January, and the streets were full of people.
scenes.say: It was strangely warm for January, and the streets were full of people.

scenes.text: Near the harbor stood a giant steel tank.
scenes.say: Near the harbor stood a giant steel tank.

scenes.text: Fifty feet tall. Ninety feet wide.
scenes.say: Fifty feet tall. Ninety feet wide.

scenes.text: Filled with two point three million gallons of molasses.
scenes.say: Filled with two point three million gallons of molasses.

scenes.text: And the neighbors had noticed something. The tank leaked.
scenes.say: [serious] And the neighbors had noticed something. The tank leaked.

scenes.text: Brown syrup oozed from its seams.
scenes.say: Brown syrup oozed from its seams.

scenes.text: The company's fix? They painted the tank brown.
scenes.say: The company's fix? [scoffs] They painted the tank brown.

scenes.text: Just after noon, people heard a deep rumble... then a rattling, like machine guns.
scenes.say: [tense] Just after noon, people heard a deep rumble... then a rattling, like machine guns.

scenes.text: That was the rivets bursting out of the steel.
scenes.say: That was the rivets bursting out of the steel.

scenes.text: And then the whole tank split open.
scenes.say: [shocked] And then the whole tank split open.

scenes.text: A wave of molasses, twenty-five feet high, rolled through the streets at about thirty-five miles an hour.
scenes.say: A wave of molasses, twenty-five feet high, rolled through the streets at about thirty-five miles an hour.

scenes.text: Faster than any person can run.
scenes.say: Faster than any person can run.

scenes.text: It knocked buildings off their foundations, smashed into the steel supports of the elevated railway,
scenes.say: It knocked buildings off their foundations, smashed into the steel supports of the elevated railway,

scenes.text: and swept up wagons, horses, and people.
scenes.say: and swept up wagons, horses, and people.

scenes.text: Twenty-one people died. Around a hundred and fifty were hurt.
scenes.say: [sad] Twenty-one people died. Around a hundred and fifty were hurt.

scenes.text: Rescuers struggled for days, because as the air cooled, the molasses grew thicker, trapping anyone caught inside.
scenes.say: Rescuers struggled for days, because as the air cooled, the molasses grew thicker, trapping anyone caught inside.

scenes.text: Investigators found the tank had been badly built and barely tested.
scenes.say: [softly] Investigators found the tank had been badly built and barely tested.

scenes.text: After that, engineers had to sign off on projects like this.
scenes.say: After that, engineers had to sign off on projects like this.

scenes.text: And locals said that for decades, on hot summer days, the neighborhood still smelled sweet.
scenes.say: [sighs] And locals said that for decades, on hot summer days, the neighborhood still smelled sweet.

scenes.text: That disaster came from cutting corners.
scenes.say: [curious] That disaster came from cutting corners.

scenes.text: Our next one came from a very careful plan... to sell something that wasn't for sale.
scenes.say: Our next one came from a very careful plan... to sell something that wasn't for sale.

scenes.text: In 1925, a smooth-talking con man named Victor Lustig read a small story in a Paris newspaper.
scenes.say: [curious] In 1925, a smooth-talking con man named Victor Lustig read a small story in a Paris newspaper.

scenes.text: The Eiffel Tower was rusting, and repairs were costing the city a fortune.
scenes.say: The Eiffel Tower was rusting, and repairs were costing the city a fortune.

scenes.text: Most people saw a news story. Lustig saw a product.
scenes.say: [sly] Most people saw a news story. Lustig saw a product.

scenes.text: He had fake government letterhead made, posing as a top official from France's Ministry of Posts and Telegraphs.
scenes.say: He had fake government letterhead made, posing as a top official from France's Ministry of Posts and Telegraphs.

scenes.text: Then he invited a handful of scrap metal dealers to one of the fanciest hotels in Paris.
scenes.say: Then he invited a handful of scrap metal dealers to one of the fanciest hotels in Paris.

scenes.text: There, he told them a secret.
scenes.say: There, he told them a secret.

scenes.text: The city was going to tear down the Eiffel Tower and sell it for scrap.
scenes.say: [whispers] The city was going to tear down the Eiffel Tower and sell it for scrap.

scenes.text: And it all had to stay quiet.
scenes.say: And it all had to stay quiet.

scenes.text: One dealer, André Poisson, wanted the deal badly.
scenes.say: [excited] One dealer, André Poisson, wanted the deal badly.

scenes.text: He was new in town and wanted to make a name for himself.
scenes.say: He was new in town and wanted to make a name for himself.

scenes.text: Then Lustig hinted that government officials don't earn very much...
scenes.say: Then Lustig hinted that government officials don't earn very much...

scenes.text: So Poisson paid him a bribe, on top of the price.
scenes.say: So Poisson paid him a bribe, on top of the price.

scenes.text: Lustig grabbed the money and caught a train to Vienna.
scenes.say: [laughs] Lustig grabbed the money and caught a train to Vienna.

scenes.text: And Poisson? He was too embarrassed to go to the police.
scenes.say: And Poisson? He was too embarrassed to go to the police.

scenes.text: Lustig watched the newspapers. Not a word.
scenes.say: [chuckles] Lustig watched the newspapers. Not a word.

scenes.text: So not long after, he came back... and tried to sell the tower again.
scenes.say: So not long after, he came back... and tried to sell the tower again.

scenes.text: This time, a dealer did go to the police, and Lustig had to run.
scenes.say: This time, a dealer did go to the police, and Lustig had to run.

scenes.text: Years later, he was caught in the United States, for printing fake money.
scenes.say: Years later, he was caught in the United States, for printing fake money.

scenes.text: But for a few days in 1925, a scrap dealer truly believed he owned the most famous tower in the world.
scenes.say: [amused] But for a few days in 1925, a scrap dealer truly believed he owned the most famous tower in the world.

scenes.text: Lustig lied, and everyone believed him.
scenes.say: [serious] Lustig lied, and everyone believed him.

scenes.text: Our last man was told the truth, again and again... and refused to believe it for twenty-nine years.
scenes.say: Our last man was told the truth, again and again... and refused to believe it for twenty-nine years.

scenes.text: In December 1944, a young Japanese officer named Hiroo Onoda was sent to Lubang, a small island in the Philippines.
scenes.say: [serious] In December 1944, a young Japanese officer named Hiroo Onoda was sent to Lubang, a small island in the Philippines.

scenes.text: His orders: keep fighting, and never surrender.
scenes.say: His orders: keep fighting, and never surrender.

scenes.text: As American forces landed, his commander, Major Yoshimi Taniguchi, made him a promise.
scenes.say: As American forces landed, his commander, Major Yoshimi Taniguchi, made him a promise.

scenes.text: Whatever happens, we'll come back for you.
scenes.say: Whatever happens, we'll come back for you.

scenes.text: A few months later, World War Two ended. But no one came.
scenes.say: A few months later, World War Two ended. [softly] But no one came.

scenes.text: Leaflets fell from planes saying the war was over. Onoda decided they were fake.
scenes.say: Leaflets fell from planes saying the war was over. Onoda decided they were fake.

scenes.text: Newspapers were left for him. Letters from his family. He believed none of it.
scenes.say: Newspapers were left for him. Letters from his family. He believed none of it.

scenes.text: So he stayed hidden in the jungle with a few other soldiers, still fighting his war.
scenes.say: [sighs] So he stayed hidden in the jungle with a few other soldiers, still fighting his war.

scenes.text: And that war was real for the people of Lubang.
scenes.say: [serious] And that war was real for the people of Lubang.

scenes.text: Over the years, Onoda's group killed local islanders. As many as thirty, by some accounts.
scenes.say: Over the years, Onoda's group killed local islanders. As many as thirty, by some accounts.

scenes.text: One by one, his companions were gone. By 1972, Onoda was alone.
scenes.say: One by one, his companions were gone. By 1972, Onoda was alone.

scenes.text: Then, in 1974, a young Japanese traveler named Norio Suzuki arrived.
scenes.say: [curious] Then, in 1974, a young Japanese traveler named Norio Suzuki arrived.

scenes.text: He'd told friends he was searching for three things: Lieutenant Onoda, a panda, and the Abominable Snowman, in that order.
scenes.say: He'd told friends he was searching for three things: Lieutenant Onoda, a panda, and the Abominable Snowman, in that order.

scenes.text: He found the first one in four days.
scenes.say: [chuckles] He found the first one in four days.

scenes.text: The two became friends. But Onoda still wouldn't come out.
scenes.say: The two became friends. But Onoda still wouldn't come out.

scenes.text: He would only stop if his commanding officer ordered him to.
scenes.say: He would only stop if his commanding officer ordered him to.

scenes.text: So Japan found Major Taniguchi, now an old man working in a bookshop, and flew him to the island.
scenes.say: [emotional] So Japan found Major Taniguchi, now an old man working in a bookshop, and flew him to the island.

scenes.text: On March 9, 1974, Taniguchi stood in front of Onoda and read him his final orders.
scenes.say: On March 9, 1974, Taniguchi stood in front of Onoda and read him his final orders.

scenes.text: The war was over.
scenes.say: The war was over.

scenes.text: Onoda handed over his sword and his rifle. It still worked.
scenes.say: [softly] Onoda handed over his sword and his rifle. It still worked.

scenes.text: He had fought for twenty-nine years, for a war that had ended long before.
scenes.say: [sad] He had fought for twenty-nine years, for a war that had ended long before.

scenes.text: And Taniguchi had promised to come back.
scenes.say: [emotional] And Taniguchi had promised to come back.

scenes.text: Twenty-nine years later... he did.
scenes.say: Twenty-nine years later... he did.

scenes.text: So, which one got you? The emus, the dancers, the syrup wave, the con man, or the soldier?
